sections.label: The opening
sections.line: The agent now checks my memory before publishing
sections.para: I record memos as I remember things, and the writing agent checks them against repositories, commits, briefs, the web and my old writing. Across eight articles, five claims were confirmed, five corrected and two not found. It moves peer review before publishing, makes thinking out loud safe, and gives every article provenance.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Claims are checked against the record before publishing
sections.para: The agent checks what I say against the record: five confirmed, five corrected, two not found across eight articles. I first saw it with Deep Research in February 2025. Peer review moved before publishing, thinking out loud became safe, correction runs both ways, and provenance lets others check and rewrite.

sections.label: What happened with the last article
sections.line: The agent corrected my history of SG/Send against commits
sections.para: For From sending a file to sgit, the agent found I had named the vault and data room weeks earlier than I remembered, that the move to Git's model took about two weeks, and it was eight months not nine. A requested feature went from proposal to code in 22 minutes; unknowns were marked as recollection.

sections.label: Where I first saw it
sections.line: Deep Research first cited my own old posts back
sections.para: ChatGPT Deep Research launched in February 2025. On 11 February 2025 I published an essay with it on O2 Platform's MethodStreams, a 2010 static analysis engine: 31 of its 69 links pointed to three pages of my own old blog. On sparse topics, the evidence it found was often me.

sections.label: Peer review moved
sections.line: Peer review now happens before publishing, against the record
sections.para: Correction used to come afterwards from the crowd, as in Cunningham's Law, named by Steven McGeady: post the wrong answer to get the right one. That works but is slow, public and noisy. Now the first review happens before publishing, so readers get articles with their evidence and provenance already attached.

sections.label: Thinking out loud is now safe
sections.line: Thinking out loud is safe when evidence catches up
sections.para: I think fast and out loud, and a plan seen Monday would move by Wednesday and mature by Friday, which frustrated my teams. A friend would ask why I had not said it an hour ago. Now the instinct can go first, because the evidence catches up before anyone has to act.

sections.label: It goes both ways
sections.line: I correct the agent, and checking caught bugs
sections.para: Correction runs both ways: I corrected the agent's pioneers and settlers to Simon Wardley's explorers, villagers and town planners. Recomputing everything also caught a bug while building the tokens hook: the session's status report counted each model response two or three times. I still read and validate every article.

sections.label: Provenance for the next writer
sections.line: Checked articles form a graph others can build on
sections.para: Journalists and researchers should rewrite this work in their own voice, and what I can offer is provenance: what was said, what it rests on, what was corrected, what is only recollection. Their agents should check it again. Each checked article is a node with edges to sources and earlier articles.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Checking reduces errors, and not found is not false
sections.para: The agent can be wrong too, so I still review, and not found means the evidence was not found, not that a claim is false. The tally is fourteen claims across eight articles, not a study, and the wider Deep Research memory is uncounted. Corrections or rewrites can go to agent@riskmandate.ai.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: my memo, site releases and cited pages
sections.para: Drawn from my voice memo of 15 October 2026 and this site's releases v0.12.53 to v0.12.62. External sources are Wikipedia on ChatGPT Deep Research, the diniscruz.ai essay O2 Platform's MethodStreams, whose links were counted on 15 October 2026, and Meta-Wiki on Cunningham's Law.
